newsitem.title: UK: UK govt makes four monetary policy appointments.
newsitem.headline: UK govt makes four monetary policy appointments.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown on Monday appointed four outside members to the Bank of England's new monetary policy committee -- Professor Charles Goodhart, Dr DeAnne Julius, Sir Alan Budd and Professor Willem Buiter.

The four will sit on the committee alongside four members from the Bank of England, led by by Governor Eddie George, until the appointment of a second deputy governor to the Bank takes its number to five.

The committee will meet for the first time to discuss interest rates on Thursday and Friday. Brown announced the shake-up to the monetary policy structure last month, giving the Bank operational independence to set interest rates for the first time.
The nine-person committee will meet each month to discuss interest rates and the government will have no vote.
"I am delighted that we have secured the services of such distinguished individuals for the Monetary Policy Committee," Brown said.

"They will bring not only recognised expertise in their own fields, but a breadth of experience of finance and industry to the making of monetary policy in this country. Their appointments...will strengthen the Bank and enhance the credibility of monetary policy in Britain."

Goodhart, 60, worked for 17 years as a monetary adviser at the Bank of England, becoming chief adviser in 1980. He is now Norman Sosnow Professor of Banking and Finance at the London School of Economics.
He and Buiter, who was born in the Netherlands in 1949 and has been Professor of International Macroeconomics at Cambridge University since 1994, will take up their posts immediately.
Julius' appointment will take effect from September 1. She has been chief economist at British Airways Plc since 1993 and chairwoman of British Airways Pension Investment Management Ltd.
Budd, 59, will be appointed when he leaves his post as Chief Economic Adviser to the Treasury, a statement said.

The new committee will be accountable to a reformed Court of the Bank of England. "In order to strengthen the capacity of the Court to exercise the role, Christopher Allsopp of Oxford University has been appointed...to join the Court," the statement said.

Brown said all the necessary interim arrangements were now in place for the Bank to take on operational responsibility for setting interest rates in order to meet the government's target of 2.5 percent for underlying inflation.

"This radical reform to monetary policy decision-making will create a platform of stability and prudent economic management for the long-term which will allow Britain to achieve high levels of growth and employment," he said.
Economists said the odds of the committee pushing official interest rates, now at 6.25 percent, higher at their first meeting were finely balanced.

In its last inflation report, the Bank said interest rates would have to rise further if the target was to be met in two years' time. Brown raised rates by a quarter-point last month, just five days into office.
